summary: Round w17 rates head 7744d1c (polish A: jShell #595d64 -> #434349, jCap #5c6066 -> #4b4b50, jShellIn #4a4d53 -> #3e3e43, jBand leather -> satin plastic layer #5d5e66). The geometry and proportion are unchanged from w16 (nested pair, shells, privacy walls, monitor walls, monument top, aisle caps), so the score rests on the two colour and finish changes. (1) Darker shells: the result is mixed and slightly positive overall. The cap tops now fall inside the photo range, with the rim sheen intact (o2 rim peak / face 1.26, was 1.15; q10 caps L108 against c_27315 L124-143 and c_27312 L113-128). The cream aisle doors now stand out against darker frames, as they do in c_27312 / c_27314. The far rows of q06 (L88-97) sit in c_27312's L74-101. The near shaded vertical faces overshoot, though: q09 wall L45 against c_27314 L72-83, q10 front face L54 against c_27315 L65-84, q06 near-left L54 against c_27312 L68-89. Ash / shell-face ratios are now 2.5-4.0 (before 1.6-2.4). I measure 1.6-2.2 on the official photos' lit faces and up to 2.7 on c_27312's darkest console boxes, and 1.8-2.0 in-flight (kn_8). The hue claim is overstated. The official shells sample h207-231 (mostly ~220, s 0.10-0.25), with only the darkest bezel and console parts at h247-256. The new material (R=G<B, h240) renders h231-235, while the old one rendered h217-221. Both are within ~12 deg at low saturation, so the hue shift is barely visible. Not going neutral was the right call: the photos render at s 0.12-0.25, and #434349 has HSV s 0.08 anyway, so it also meets the integrator's limit. (2) jBand on the satin layer clearly helps. At the hand-off camera (o1, cruise) the band's local contrast falls from hp 0.154 to 0.034, against a target of <=0.04 (kn_8 band 0.024). The hammered-metal dimples are gone, leaving a faint orange-peel stipple. The band L96 h237 in q10 is close to c_27315's padded band (L106 h248). Net: same product, minor value and material differences. I stay at 8.5 with one medium issue: the shaded near faces are too dark, partly from the cabin AO.

issues.detail: Shaded near shell faces now too dark; the ash-to-shell value ratio overshoots
issues.problem: The new jShell value is right for the lit caps and the far rows, but the large near vertical faces, which sit in cabin AO and shadow, drop to ~0.6-0.8x the photos. In q09 the privacy wall reads close to black-slate instead of the mid charcoal of c_27314. The ash / face ratio is 2.5-4.0, against 1.6-2.2 on the lit faces of the official photos (up to 2.7 on c_27312's darkest console boxes) and 1.8-2.0 in kn_8.
issues.fix: Split the difference on the face material only, and keep jCap (the cap tops and rims are in range). In src/09_seats.js:83, set jShell c '#434349' -> '#4a4b51' (about +10 %, h ~230). Leave jShellIn (line 84) as is, since its faces are the inner shadowed ones. Hand the rest to lighting: the AO and crevice term on large vertical shell faces above 0.75 m (12_scene.js). Re-measure q09 so the wall reaches L60-70 while q06 far rows stay at or below L100.

issues.detail: Shell hue drifted from slate toward blue-violet
issues.problem: The official shells sample h207-231 (mostly ~220), and only the darkest bezel and console bits reach h247-256. The R=G<B material (h240) renders h231-235; before it rendered h217-221. The shift is barely visible at s ~0.15, but the code comment's 'violet-grey' overstates what the photos show.
issues.fix: If you touch the value per the medium issue, also put G just above R: jShell '#4a4b51' and jCap '#4b4c51' (09_seats.js:83/85), which give h ~225-230 rendered. Correct the comment to 'cool slate-grey (h~220), darkest parts violet'.
